LABOR_CHANGE announcement category and alert hover source

This directory records native source extraction, not a game-screen observation
or a translation test. Enum names come from the checked-in df-structures XML;
all numeric routes come from the configured Windows PE images.

Category boundary
  reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000, map RVA eaa20..eab13
  classic   PE:6a70b91c:0270a000, map RVA ea9b0..eaaa3

The mapper sign-extends announcement_type (int16 at descriptor+0), compares
the resulting value unsigned against 353, and returns GENERAL for values
outside 0..353. The 354-byte native remap selects a 34-entry RVA jump table.
route-table.tsv reads all enum values 0..355 from those actual table bytes,
including the two final values' default route. No spelling of the displayed
profession is used to choose an alert category.

Exactly two input values select the remap entry 25 / return 11 LABOR_CHANGE:
  236 PROFESSION_CHANGES
    reference producer 133bcf0, submit 133c0c0
    classic producer 1336c60, submit 1337030
  283 CITIZEN_BECOMES_NONSOLDIER
    reference producer 1374fc0, submit 1375142
    classic producer 136ff30, submit 13700b2
The instruction listings retain the complete mapper; pe-*-ghidra-decompiled.c
are actual Ghidra 12.1.4 output. The tool's generated adventure_choice_ prefix
is only a script naming convention. Its switch override is populated from the
recovered native jump table, not from hand-selected LABOR_CHANGE examples.

FORT_POSITION_SUCCESSION (178) instead maps to NOBLE (7).
CITIZEN_BECOMES_SOLDIER (282) maps to MILITARY (12).
These do not add body alternatives to this LABOR_CHANGE group. A source
containing a noble title such as baron does not change its producer type.
The two actual body producers and all of their name/profession suppliers are
handled by the companion noble/profession extraction. Their finite sentence
branches plus typed RAW and user-authored fields form the complete source
grammar; generated names cannot be enumerated as a finite string list.

Actual Ghidra hover output retained in place
  data/extracted/fortress-rectangle/pe-reference-placement-renderer-owner.c
  data/extracted/fortress-rectangle/pe-classic-placement-renderer-owner.c
These are the entire monolithic Fortress renderers, from 3d6950 / 3d4510
through 3fca34 / 3fa5f4; trailing jump-table data are excluded from code.
The corresponding full PE unwind instruction listings remain in
data/extracted/fortress-alert-ui/*-alert-hover-renderer.asm.

Individual alert hover body
  Reference 3f6351 selects the actual announcement_alertst pointer.
  A changed selected pointer, or width other than 80, rebuilds the cache.
  The alert+8 report-ID vector is resolved against world.status.reports.
  A missing report ID contributes no text.
  For each present report, report.text at report+8 is the whole source.
  report.repeat_count at +34 <= 0 keeps the source unchanged.
  repeat_count > 0 copies the source and appends " x" and the signed int32
  decimal result of repeat_count+1 (3f6427..3f6477).
  Native word wrapping occurs after this whole-source construction.
  Its colors (+28) and brightness (+2a) are copied per resulting row.
  The row loop draws only the cached range that fits within the hover frame.
  It does not author or translate an additional report sentence.
  Classic code addresses for these hover blocks are reference minus 2440.

The red ALERT-button hover is a separate source path: it walks the global
alert_button_announcement_id vector, uses the same report lookup and whole
source/repeat construction (reference 3d7505..3d7555), and has no unit-summary
loop. It is not an additional LABOR_CHANGE producer.

Hover instruction and visibility branches
  The existing screenshot instruction has the exact source:
    Left click for recenter and expand options.  Right click to dismiss.
  The two occurrences are at reference 3fab2b (ALERT button) and 3fae1b
  (individual icon), classic 3f86eb / 3f89db.
  The renderer suppresses both hovers while the alert popup is open or the
  modal announcement-popup vector is nonempty. Native widget/instruction
  priority can also suppress them. A successful button-hover draw jumps past
  the icon-hover path, so these two hover frames are mutually exclusive.
  Both complete captions already use data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv.

Expanded popup: retained actual Ghidra output
  data/extracted/announcement-popup-native/renderer/reference-40d5f0.c
  data/extracted/announcement-popup-native/renderer/classic-40b1b0.c
  The source order is viewing_unit, else viewing_alert_button, else selected
  alert. All use complete stored report.text and the same repeat semantics.
  With no owner there is no body or instruction source.
  viewing_unit, alert_button, or selected alert without unit IDs:
    You can recenter on certain announcements.  Right click to close.
  selected alert with a nonempty unit-ID vector:
    Select a report to view the full text.  Right click to close.
  Both complete captions are already in data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv.
  The matching input C bodies (reference-40f780.c/classic-40d340.c) cover
  closing, recentering and report selection and author no further text.

Shared renderer branches, not additional labor-report productions
  The generic icon-hover and popup paths also support unit/category summary
  vectors for their other alert groups. Category 0/1/2 appends fighting!,
  sparring., hunting. after capitalized unit identity + " is ". Any other
  category adds no verb. Only hover substitutes Somebody when unit lookup
  fails; popup skips the missing unit. decompiled-ui-productions.tsv retains
  these shared renderer branches so that they are not misidentified as a new
  LABOR_CHANGE sentence or as a new profession branch.

No game UI, input, hot reload, loaded-module state or runtime log was accessed.
